data.name: Spooky Heroes
data.detailed_description:
Play as a knight who tries to unveil the mystery behind the spooky events occurring lately : Undead rising at night, hordes of goblins, orcs, tritons, elves, yetis and heretics suddenly becoming hostile, monstrous creatures blocking the path of travelers... Enroll new heroes on the way, each with their own powers and way to play. Earn money by slaying monsters, completing quests or finding treasure chests and spent it in villages to buy items which will help you on your journey. Be careful at night as foul horrors will rise and block your path. Ride boats and dragons, explore underwater caves and travel in more unique locations in this 2D casual platform game.

Features :
  • 9 unique heroes with 3 basic powers, 1 ultimate power and 1 passive each.
  • 19 unique stages and 5 villages to explore
  • Dynamic day and night cycle
  • Dynamic monsters spawn & traps
  • Earn money by solving quests, killing enemies and boss or finding chests
  • 22 enemies with their own powers and passives (18 of them being playable too)
  • 13 boss with their unique powers and strategies
  • 22 quests to solve split in 5 main categories : Hunt, Timed Collect, Slay & Collect, Race, Ambush
  • 21 unique items to help you on your journey
  • 3 unique vehicles to ride + 1 baby dragon !
  • 2 players in local coop
  • Keyboard keys customization (but controller is HIGHLY advised)
  • Controller support (and HIGHLY advised)
  • Survival mode with 2 sub modes :
    • Cooperation where 2 players must survive as many waves as possible
    • Competition mode where the second player can control any monsters on screen and must defeat the first player as soon as possible
  • Each village offers 5 buildings :
    • The smith to buy armors
    • The item shop to buy item unique to each village
    • The restaurant to buy food to heal yourself on your journey
    • The bank to store your hard earned money
    • The inn to sleep till night or morning

reviews.review:
Spooky Heroes is a fantasy-themed 2D action platformer that attempts to deliver much more than a conventional side-scrolling adventure. Developed and published by Gaweb Studio, the game combines monster battles, character recruitment, exploration, equipment management, and cooperative multiplayer within a world troubled by supernatural disturbances. Players assume the role of a knight investigating mysterious events that have transformed once-peaceful regions into dangerous territories populated by undead creatures and hostile fantasy races. Although the overall presentation is relatively modest, the game distinguishes itself through an unusually extensive collection of gameplay features that provide different ways to approach its adventure.

One of its most interesting qualities is the selection of playable characters. Rather than limiting the experience to a single protagonist, the game allows players to recruit nine heroes, each equipped with three basic abilities, an ultimate power, and a passive skill. This system introduces flexibility into combat and encourages experimentation with different fighting styles. The inclusion of playable monsters further expands the available options, with 18 creatures offering alternative ways to experience the action. While the sheer number of characters is appealing, the effectiveness of this variety ultimately depends on how distinct and balanced their abilities feel during actual encounters.

Combat is an essential part of the experience, featuring 22 enemy types and 13 bosses with different abilities and attack patterns. The mixture of ordinary enemies and more demanding opponents creates opportunities to test character powers and adjust strategies. The game also introduces environmental hazards, traps, and dynamically appearing monsters that can complicate exploration. However, players seeking exceptionally precise combat mechanics or sophisticated enemy behavior may find the experience comparatively basic. Its strength lies in offering numerous combat possibilities rather than perfecting one particularly elaborate fighting system.

Exploration takes place across 19 stages and five villages, providing a combination of platforming challenges, dangerous environments, and opportunities to collect valuable resources. Players can investigate underwater caves, navigate hazardous areas, and travel using boats, dragons, and other vehicles. The dynamic day-and-night cycle adds another consideration, as dangerous creatures become more prominent after darkness falls. This mechanic makes traveling at different times potentially meaningful and contributes to the game's supernatural atmosphere. Nevertheless, the environmental variety may not completely eliminate repetition for players who prefer carefully structured levels with continually evolving challenges.

The quest system introduces additional objectives through 22 assignments distributed across hunting, timed collection, slaying and gathering, racing, and ambush activities. Completing these tasks rewards players with resources and money that can be invested in equipment and useful items. Villages function as preparation areas where players can purchase armor from blacksmiths, obtain supplies, eat restorative food, store currency, and rest at inns. These activities provide a light role-playing structure that complements the platforming action. Although the economic systems are not especially complex, they give players practical reasons to revisit settlements and manage their resources between adventures.

Multiplayer is another noteworthy attraction. Two players can cooperate locally, combining different heroes and abilities while progressing through challenges. The survival modes provide additional entertainment beyond the main campaign, particularly the competitive variation in which one participant controls monsters and attempts to overwhelm the other player. This asymmetric concept is a welcome departure from traditional competitive multiplayer and gives the game a playful quality. Cooperative survival, meanwhile, emphasizes teamwork against waves of increasingly dangerous enemies. These options can improve replayability, especially for players who enjoy sharing smaller independent games with friends.

The visual presentation follows a simple fantasy style that prioritizes recognizable characters and environments over elaborate graphical effects. Its straightforward appearance fits the casual nature of the adventure, although it may seem dated beside more visually sophisticated platformers. The game's accessible system requirements are an advantage, making it suitable for less powerful computers. Controller input is strongly recommended, while customizable keyboard controls provide an alternative. Steam achievements and trading cards offer additional incentives for players who enjoy completing secondary objectives.

Steam Deck compatibility remains Unknown or Unverified, as no official Verified or Playable classification is displayed. Its Linux support, lightweight requirements, and controller functionality are promising characteristics, but they do not guarantee reliable performance on Valve's handheld. Players should be prepared for possible control adjustments or compatibility issues.

Ultimately, Spooky Heroes is an ambitious but relatively unrefined independent adventure whose greatest strength is the amount of content packed into its modest framework. The playable heroes, varied monsters, multiple exploration areas, and unusual competitive survival mode give it a personality of its own. However, repetitive objectives, basic presentation, and potentially uneven gameplay depth may limit its appeal. It is best suited to players who value experimentation, casual fantasy combat, and cooperative entertainment over exceptional polish. 

Rating: 5/10
